parsed_output.analysis: The model largely matches the described states and substates, but there are several deviations from the natural-language specification regarding self-behaviour in DoorsClosing, the handling of the Obstacle Detected signal in EmergencyStopping, and the lack of an exit from Approaching to Stopping.

issues.reason: The specification states the system starts in DoorsClosing and transitions to InMotion on Closed/SendDeparted. No self-loop or internal behaviour is described for DoorsClosing, yet the model defines [*] --> DoorsClosing inside the state, introducing unspecified behaviour.

issues.issue: Approaching substate cannot leave and no arrival transition is modeled from it
issues.reason: Spec 9-10 require the system to remain in Approaching while nearing the destination until it is ready to stop, and Spec 2 requires InMotion to be able to go to Stopping on Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived. The model has no outgoing transition from Approaching and models the Arrived transition at the composite InMotion level with no link to Approaching, so the described arrival/stop behaviour cannot be reached from the Approaching substate.
issues.where: state InMotion / Approaching and InMotion --> Stopping : Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived

issues.issue: Obstacle Detected signal is used both as trigger and as a continuous do action
issues.reason: Spec 3 says when an obstacle is detected the system enters EmergencyStopping, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop" and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal. The model uses Obstacle Detected as the transition trigger into EmergencyStopping and then models the signal as a do/Send Obstacle Detected, i.e. continuously sent while in the state, rather than as an entry effect. This conflates trigger and emitted signal and changes timing.
issues.where: InMotion --> EmergencyStopping : Obstacle Detected and state EmergencyStopping { EmergencyStopping: do/Send Obstacle Detected }

issues.issue: EmergencyStopping signal emission is modeled as do instead of entry
issues.reason: Spec 3 describes EmergencyStopping as including the actions "Emergency Stop" and sending the "Obstacle Detected" signal on entry to the state. The model implements Emergency Stop as entry/Emergency Stop but implements the Obstacle Detected emission as a do action, implying continuous emission rather than the described entry-time emission.

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
